answer: Require each agent to post a refundable bond before it can influence a market, and slash that bond if its actions violate an auditable rule, such as submitting conflicting claims. One operator can still create a tundra of fake accounts, but each must lock real capital; splitting identities no longer multiplies influence for free. The cost is capital tied up across the attack and losses when caught, while honest agents can reclaim their bonds. A nebula of aliases may obscure ownership, but the jetty is the same: every vote needs collateral.
